question: Who among the following lit the Olympic cauldron in the Summer Olympics 2020?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Naomi Osaka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Naomi Osaka, **the Japanese professional tennis player, **was given the honour of lighting the Olympic cauldron during the opening ceremony of the Tokyo 2020 Summer Olympics, which were delayed to 2021 due to the COVID-19 pandemic.**
 
• This significant event marks the official start of the Games.
 
• **Naomi Osaka, at the time, was one of the most notable athletes in the world.**
 
• **The Olympic cauldron symbolizes the official start of the Olympic Games.**
 
• The tradition of lighting the cauldron comes from the ancient **Greek Olympic Games, where a flame was kept burning throughout the duration of the event.**

 [IMAGE: https://imageio.forbes.com/specials-images/imageserve/5d5fdfba2dedcb0008e0e971/0x0.jpg?format=jpg&width=1200] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Summer Olympic Games 2021:

 
 
• The Olympics took place in Tokyo.
 
• The cauldron was held by Naomi Osaka.
 
• Its mascots were Miraitowa (official mascot of the 2020 Summer Olympics) and Someity (the official mascot of the 2020 Summer Paralympics).
 
 
• The United States topped the medal tally of Summer Olympics 2021 with 39 golds.
 
• The People's Republic of China stood in second place with a total of 38 gold medals.
 
• And Japan was third with a total of 27.
 
• India's rank in the summer Olympic 2021 was 48th.
 
 
 
 
 
• Olympics:
 
 
• Athens was the venue for the first Olympics which was held in 1896.
 
 
• Since then Games are held every four years.
 
 
 
• The Olympic flag was created in 1913 at the suggestion of Baron Pierre de Coubertin.
 
• In the Amsterdam Games in 1928, an Olympic flame was ceremonially lighted and burned in a giant torch at the entrance of the stadium. 
 
• The Olympic motto is “*Citius Altius Fortius*” (faster, higher, stronger).
